# Traefik — load-balancer

Two backends behind one router with sticky sessions via a ROUTEID cookie that Traefik synthesizes itself, so the backends need no Tomcat jvmRoute. APP_NAME distinguishes which one served the page.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Traefik dynamic config (`vaadin.yml`), mounted into
`/etc/traefik/dynamic`:

```yaml
# Two backends behind one router, with sticky sessions.
#
# Vaadin needs affinity: the session lives in one backend's memory, so a
# request that lands on the other one finds no UI. Traefik synthesizes its own
# affinity cookie rather than reading a route id out of JSESSIONID, so — as
# with the NGINX sibling — the backends need no Tomcat jvmRoute. APP_NAME is
# what distinguishes them in the rendered page.
#
# The first request carries no cookie and is load-balanced normally, which is
# why CI warms both backends before the tests: a cold JVM answering a browser's
# first render can exceed the test timeout.
http:
  routers:
    vaadin:
      rule: PathPrefix(`/`)
      entryPoints:
        - web
      middlewares:
        - compress
      service: vaadin

  services:
    vaadin:
      loadBalancer:
        sticky:
          cookie:
            name: ROUTEID
            path: /
            httpOnly: true
        servers:
          - url: http://vaadin-1:8080
          - url: http://vaadin-2:8080

  middlewares:
    compress:
      compress:
        excludedContentTypes:
          - text/event-stream
          - text/plain
```

The entryPoints and the file provider come from the shared
[traefik.yml](../../traefik.yml), mounted read-only.
